speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what the rash looks like on your scalp and forehead, and when did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash itch significantly, and are there similar scaly patches on the baby's diaper area or skin folds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any other areas of the body affected by this rash, particularly the skin folds behind the ears or in the armpits? Does the baby seem uncomfortable or itchy due to the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal culture results and the characteristic greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead of an infant, this presentation is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap. I will not ask further questions as the clinical picture is distinct from psoriasis or infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis
